item.title: Madang Governor challenges National Government to upgrade Gaubin Hospital
item.description: Madang Governor Ramsey Pariwa has challenged the National Government to upgrade Gaubin Hospital on Karkar Island to a Level 4 facility, describing the hospital as a lifeline for Sumkar District. Governor Pariwa made the call while presenting a cheque of K1,281,272.36 to Sumkar MP Alex Sunguman during Prime Minister James Marape’s visit to the district for the commissioning of projects. item.title: Prime Minister Marape Congratulates Kikita 1 Ward Councillor
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has congratulated Ms Susan Tumbaria, Councillor for Kikita 1 Ward in the Tari Urban Local Level Government, on her outstanding achievement as the only woman councillor to secure a second term. The Prime Minister commended her resilience, leadership and commitment to public service, describing her re-election as a powerful example of women earning the confidence of their communities through hard work, integrity and dedication. item.title: Dei Council ballot counting suspended due to heavy rain
item.description: COUNTING of ballot papers for the Dei Council election in the Western Highlands Province was suspended due to wet conditions. The rain poured on Saturday night and continued, and stopped around 10 am, which prevented the counting officials, scrutineers, and security forces from counting. item.title: K198.8 Million frozen under Proceeds Of Crime Legislation
item.description: Commissioner of Police, David Manning, has announced that almost 200 million Kina has been frozen in bank accounts as part of an investigation into one of the country's most serious cases of fraud. The Asset Restraint and Recovery Working Group (ARROW), working under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2022, has successfully frozen 198.8 million Kina across multiple bank accounts relating to the matter. item.title: Prime Minister Marape directs review of Mining Agreements amid record commodity prices
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has directed the Treasury Department and the Internal Revenue Commission (IRC) to undertake a comprehensive review of all mining agreements in Papua New Guinea, following record global increases in gold, silver and copper prices. The Prime Minister said the surge in commodity prices presents an opportunity for the nation to secure fair and equitable returns from the extraction of its natural resources.
